notes: Generated by tools/tubuild.py create, then reconciled by hand and extended through the adjacent factory.

Two legacy shards declared DecIfAbove0_Short with different return types (void in State0, unsigned short in State2). The value-returning form is kept as the more complete observation; both call sites compile against it unchanged and all 16 functions still reproduce.

The destructor body is NOT written in the TU. include/daObjTbox_c.h now defines `~daObjTbox_c() {}` inline: from an inline body mwccarm emits D1 then D0 -- the cartridge's order -- and no leaf D2. With the body out of line in the TU the same two bodies come out D0-before-D1 and the isolation step refuses the object.

The factory is now a plain `new daObjTbox_c()`. It previously had to spell the allocation as a direct call to the mangled fBase_c::operator new, because without a leaf operator new in scope `new daObjTbox_c` reached for the global one and left an unresolved allocator relocation; the header now declares that leaf, so the ROM's own allocator call is what the compiler emits.
No static initializer is claimed: the module-wide sinit inventory does not narrow an owner to this class TU, and the three pointer-to-member pairs at data_ov064_0211c98c stay under legacy ownership.

The manifest licenses only the 16-function .text interval. Compiler-emitted RTTI, type-name and vtable records are exact deadstrip-data checks against canonical ROM addresses; production keeps the retail metadata band under legacy ownership.
